arxiv-2104-11524.title: Intermittency analysis of proton numbers in heavy-ion collisions at energies available at the BNL Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider
arxiv-2104-11524.creator: Jin Wu, Yufu Lin, Zhiming Li, Xiaofeng Luo, Yuanfang Wu
arxiv-2104-11524.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jin Wu, Yufu Lin, Zhiming Li, Xiaofeng Luo, Yuanfang Wu. Local density fluctuations near the QCD critical point has been suggested to exhibit a power-law behavior which can be probed by an intermittency analysis on scaled factorial moment (SFM) in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. The collision energy and centrality dependence of the second-order SFMs are systematically investigated in Au + + Au collisions at s N ​ N \sqrt{s_{NN}} = 7.7, 11.5, 19.6, 27, 39, 62.4, and 200 GeV within the UrQMD model.

arxiv-2109-04291.description: Abstract 1. On the model-theoretic side, we further provides mathematical structures that evaluates the language (semantic models). Among these, syntax is perhaps the easiest part.

arxiv-2205-14095.title: Is the ( g − 2 ) μ (g-2)_{\mu} anomaly a threat to Lepton Flavor Conservation?
arxiv-2205-14095.creator: Julie Pagès
arxiv-2205-14095.description: Abstract Although the ( g − 2 ) μ (g-2)_{\mu} anomaly can be explained by New Physics (NP) involving only muons, a more general flavor structure is usually expected for NP operators in the Standard Model (SM) Effective Field Theory (SMEFT).

arxiv-2307-08097.title: EasyTPP: Towards Open Benchmarking Temporal Point Processes
arxiv-2307-08097.creator: Siqiao Xue, Xiaoming Shi, Zhixuan Chu, Yan Wang, Hongyan Hao, Fan Zhou, Caigao Jiang, Chen Pan, James Y. Zhang, Qingsong Wen, Jun Zhou
arxiv-2307-08097.description: Abstract Continuous-time event sequences play a vital role in real-world domains such as healthcare, finance, online shopping, social networks, and so on. To model such data, temporal point processes (TPPs) have emerged as the most natural and competitive models, making a significant impact in both academic and application communities.

arxiv-2311-11245.title: Apparent effect of dust extinction on the observed outflow velocity of ionized gas in galaxy mergers ASURA ( Saitoh et al. 2008 ; Saitoh et al. 2009 ; Saitoh & Makino 2013 ) , AGAMA ( Vasiliev 2019 )
arxiv-2311-11245.creator: Naomichi Yutani, Yoshiki Toba, Keiichi Wada
arxiv-2311-11245.description: Abstract In this study, we examine photoionization outflows during the late stages of galaxy mergers, with a specific focus on the relation between observed velocity of outflowing gas and the apparent effects of dust extinction. We used the N-body/smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) code ASURA for galaxy merger simulations.

arxiv-2311-14163.title: Interactions in the IKKT matrix model on covariant quantum spacetime
arxiv-2311-14163.creator: & Tung Tran
arxiv-2311-14163.description: Abstract We study the interactions of the higher-spin gauge theory arising from the IKKT matrix model on a covariant quantum FLRW quantum space-time ℳ 𝙹 1 , 3 \mathcal{M}^{1,3}_{\mathtt{J}} , denoted as HS-IKKT. In particular, we elaborate some of the vertices and observe that they are not manifestly Lorentz invariant in the unitary formulation.

arxiv-2403-03503.title: Universality of pseudo-Goldstone damping near critical points
arxiv-2403-03503.creator: Yang-yang Tan, Yong-rui Chen, Wei-jie Fu, Wei-Jia Li
arxiv-2403-03503.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Yang-yang Tan, Yong-rui Chen, Wei-jie Fu, Wei-Jia Li. Real-time dynamics of strongly correlated systems, in particular its critical dynamics near phase transitions, have been always on the cutting edge of studies in diverse fields of physics, e.g., high energy physics, condensed matter, holography, etc. In this work, we investigate the critical damping of collective modes associated with spontaneous breaking of approximate symmetries, which are called pseudo-Goldstone modes, in strongly correlated systems.

arxiv-2410-17511.title: Time and Frequency Synergy for Source-Free Time-Series Domain Adaptations
arxiv-2410-17511.creator: Muhammad Tanzil Furqon, Mahardhika Pratama, Ary Shiddiqi, Lin Liu, Habibullah Habibullah, Kutluyil Dogancay
arxiv-2410-17511.description: Abstract The issue of source-free time-series domain adaptations still gains scarce research attentions. On the other hand, existing approaches rely solely on time-domain features ignoring frequency components providing complementary information. This paper proposes Time Frequency Domain Adaptation (TFDA), a method to cope with the source-free time-series domain adaptation problems.

arxiv-2507-21270.title: Generative imaging for radio interferometry with fast uncertainty quantification
arxiv-2507-21270.creator: Matthijs Mars, 1,2 Tobías I. Liaudat, 3 Jessica J. Whitney, 1 Marta M. Betcke, 4 Jason D. McEwen 1,5 1 Mullard Space Science Laboratory (MSSL), University College London (UCL), Dorking RH5 6NT, UK 2 Leiden Observatory, Leiden University, Leiden 2333 CC, The Netherlands 3 IRFU, CEA, Université Paris-
arxiv-2507-21270.description: Abstract With the rise of large radio interferometric telescopes, particularly the SKA, there is a growing demand for computationally efficient image reconstruction techniques. Existing reconstruction methods, such as the CLEAN algorithm or proximal optimisation approaches, are iterative in nature, necessitating a large amount of compute. These methods either provide no uncertainty quantification or require large computational overhead to do so.

arxiv-2509-11114.title: WildSmoke: Ready-to-Use Dynamic 3D Smoke Assets from a Single Video in the Wild
arxiv-2509-11114.creator: Yuqiu Liu Jialin Song Manolis Savva Wuyang Chen Simon Fraser University {yuqiu_liu, jialin_song, msavva, wuyang_chen}@sfu.ca
arxiv-2509-11114.description: Abstract We propose a pipeline to extract and reconstruct dynamic 3D smoke assets from a single in-the-wild video , and further integrate interactive simulation for smoke design and editing. Recent developments in 3D vision have significantly improved reconstructing and rendering fluid dynamics, supporting realistic and temporally consistent view synthesis.

arxiv-2512-12362.title: Asymmetric Laplace distribution regression model for fitting heterogeneous longitudinal response
arxiv-2512-12362.creator: Antoine Barbieri, Angelo Alcaraz, Mouna Abed, Hugues de Courson, Hélène Jacqmin-Gadda
arxiv-2512-12362.description: Abstract The systematic collection of longitudinal data is very common in practice, making mixed models widely used. Most developments around these models focus on modeling the mean trajectory of repeated measurements, typically under the assumption of homoskedasticity. However, as data become increasingly rich through intensive collection over time, these models can become limiting and may introduce biases in analysis.

arxiv-2602-21830.title: Flat Bands from Diffraction in Periodic Systems
arxiv-2602-21830.creator: Joel Lehikoinen, Rebecca Heilmann, Aron J. J. Dahlberg, Eero Härmä, Malek Mahmoudi, Arpan Dutta, Konstantinos S. Daskalakis, Päivi Törmä
arxiv-2602-21830.description: Abstract Periodic photonic structures enable precise control over the light–matter interaction through band structure engineering. Certain lattice geometries exhibit dispersionless flat bands, characterized by vanishing group velocity and diverging density of states, which present unique opportunities for applications such as slow light, nonlinear optical processes and controlling photoluminescence.

pmc-11420951.creator: Imran
pmc-11420951.description: Despite the record-high efficiency of GaAs solar cells, their terrestrial application is limited due to both the particularly high costs related to the required single-crystal substrates and epitaxial growth. A water-soluble lift-off layer could reduce costs by avoiding the need for toxic and dangerous etchants, substrate repolishing, and expensive process steps.

pmc-12592060.title: Predicting re-fracture risk factors in older adult osteoporotic vertebral fractures patients with comorbidities: development and validation of nomogram
pmc-12592060.creator: Bao Qi, Qingquan Wu, Guowu Chen, Lu Zhang, Chunyang Meng, Wei Wei, Hong Wang, Qingwei Li
pmc-12592060.description: BackgroundOsteoporotic vertebral compression fractures (OVCFs) pose a significant health burden in older adult populations, with postoperative re-fracture (re.fra) complicating recovery. Existing models (e.g., FRAX, QFracture) inadequately address comorbidities and modifiable lifestyle factors. This study aimed to develop and validate a novel nomogram integrating these underrecognized yet critical predictors for personalized risk stratification.

pmc-12652546.title: Mild Cognitive Impairment and Sarcopenia: Effects of Resistance Exercise Training on Neuroinflammation, Cognitive Performance, and Structural Brain Changes
pmc-12652546.creator: Valeria Oporto-Colicoi, Alexis Sepúlveda-Lara, Gabriel Nasri Marzuca-Nassr, Paulina Sepúlveda-Figueroa
pmc-12652546.description: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and sarcopenia are prevalent age-related conditions that often coexist and share common mechanisms such as chronic inflammation, reduced neuroplasticity, and impaired muscle function. Resistance exercise training (RET) has emerged as a promising non-pharmacological strategy capable of addressing both physical and cognitive decline.

pmc-12666589.title: The impact of pathological fluctuations versus biological variation on the interpretation of laboratory values
pmc-12666589.creator: Ariel Mundo Ortiz, Jean-Philippe Emond, Vincent Weng-Jy Cheung, Sahar Saeed, Philippe Desmarais, François Larivière, Pierre-Olivier Hétu, Robert Goulden, Quoc Dinh Nguyen
pmc-12666589.description: ObjectivesThe current criterion used to determine whether the reference interval (RI) can be used for interpretation is based on the index of individuality (II), estimated using biological variation (BV). We hypothesized that pathological variation (PV), the shift between healthy and unhealthy states, varies across biomarkers and may be considered for interpretation with BV.

pmc-13239412.title: Protective Role of Ziziphus lotus Fruits and Leaves Extracts Towards BPA‐Associated Testis Toxicity
pmc-13239412.creator: Dhekra Grami, Soumaya Wahabi, Raja Jouini, Imen Hlel, Naoures Ochi, Slimen Selmi, Hichem Sebai, Luca De Toni
pmc-13239412.description: Ziziphus lotus L. is used in folk medicine for various ailments. This study investigated the potential protective effects of aqueous extracts from the fruit (ZLFAE) and leaves (ZLLAE) of Z. lotus against testicular toxicity associated with Bisphenol A (BPA) exposure in a rat experimental model.
